newsitem.title: USA: USAir wants BA as equity holder, but not on board.
newsitem.headline: USAir wants BA as equity holder, but not on board.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Tuesday it welcomed British Airways Plc as an equity holder but wanted its estranged partner off its board.
"BA's a terrific shareholder. But will the Justice Department allow BA to sit on our board, my guess is 'no,'" USAir chairman Stephen Wolf said during a presentation before industry analysts.
Wolf also denied speculation that the carrier was seeking to force British Airways to relinquish its 24.6 percent stake in USAir.
"It's not true that we're trying to move their shares to someone else," Wolf said.
Three years ago, BA gained a minority stake in USAir and three seats on the carrier's board of directors in exchange for a $300 million capital infusion.
"If they had not given us that money, we would not be here today," Wolf said.
The relationship between the two carries became strained when Britsh Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines announced plans for a rival marketing agreement.

Since then, USAir said it would end its code-sharing alliance with BA in March 1997. USAir also sued BA and American, saying their proposed alliance would lead to a monopoly of air travel between the United States and Britain.
USAir said it expected U.S. regulators would require BA representatives to retire from its board if the proposal deal with American Airlines was finalized.
"BA's position on our board threatens our ability to compete," said USAir's corporate counsel Lawrence Nagin.
"BA's minority stake in USAir limits our ability to compete for Heathrow, since we're still considered part of the BA family," Nagin said, referring to London's main airport.
"We're recognizing that the relationship with British Airways is over. To compete to London's Heathrow Airport, we'll have to be on our own," Nagin said.
USAir has filed for access to London Heathrow airport, which could become available if a new Anglo-U.S. air treaty was agreed.
Nagin told Reuters after an analysts' presentation that USAir would not object to BA's equity stake being transferred into a non-voting trust.
